question.knowledge_point: Parametrizing a Vertical Parabola Whose Vertex Is at the Origin
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097284/assets/3f1e86d5eebc6e36b4e4087dbdead613f45be89936651f529797c3faa331e99b.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
question.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(6,9).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(6,9),$ we can substitute $x=6$ and $y=9$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}6=2pt \\ 9=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =2pt \\ 3 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{3}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & =p{(\frac{3}{p})}^{2} \\ 9 & =p\cdot \frac{9}{{p}^{2}} \\ 9 & =\frac{9}{p} \\ p & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(1)t,\,y=(1){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=2t,\,y={t}^{2}.
$$

judgment.reasoning: The earlier mathematical answers remain supported by the captured solutions. q-106411 has an authored selection error: both options 1 and 4 generate the entire parabola y=x²/4. Option 4 is option 1 with its parameter replaced by twice the parameter. The worked solution explicitly supports option 1, which remains the recommended selection, but the radio question has two mathematically correct choices. All other selected equations and values are confirmed by their own worked solutions. q-14191: setting y=0 gives 13x=2. q-73769: setting x=0 gives (y−13)(y+7)=0. q-79301: the vertex and supplied point give (y+1)²=4(x+4), hence y=−5 or 3 at x=0. q-79299: they give (x+4)²=2(y+4), hence y=4 at x=0. q-75314: the areas are 15/2 and 4, totaling 23/2. q-102668: substituting t=2x+5 gives y=4x(x+5)(2x+1). q-24378: cos(2t)=1−2sin²(t) gives the selected equation; the exact parametrized curve also requires −2≤x≤2, which the source omits. q-155954: trapezoid and triangle areas give 3/2+4=11/2. q-155955: trapezoid and rectangle areas give 6+2=8. q-90780: the net rate is 14+4t, so accumulation from the initial 100 gives 100+14t+2t². q-117666: splitting the integral at −1 gives 64+20=84. q-353388: rectangle area 12 plus semicircle area 2π gives 12+2π; the single-point discontinuity does not affect the integral. q-106419: x=t²/2 and y=t give y²=2x and cover the full parabola. q-84715: x=−3t²/2 and y=−3t give y²=−6x and cover the full parabola. q-84738: t=6x and t²=12y give x²=y/3. No captured grade establishes whether MA accepts the additional valid option in q-106411.
